title: Rainfall between two days
prompt:
A weather station logs one rainfall reading per day. Answer many questions of the form "how much rain fell from day lo to day hi, inclusive?". Return one total per query, in order.

- readings has 1 to 100,000 integers between 0 and 10,000.
- queries has 0 to 100,000 pairs [lo, hi] with 0 <= lo <= hi < len(readings).
- Return a list of integers, one per query.
hints: Summing each range with a loop costs O(length) per query. With many queries that adds up fast.
Build prefix once, where prefix[k] is the total of the first k readings, so prefix[0] = 0.
The total from lo to hi is prefix[hi + 1] - prefix[lo]. Each query becomes one subtraction.

solution.explanation: One pass builds running totals with a leading 0. A range total is the running total at its end minus the running total just before its start. The leading 0 means a range that starts at day 0 needs no special case.

complexity.notes: O(n) to build the prefix list, then O(1) per query.

followUps: Readings can now change between queries. What breaks, and what structure would you reach for?
How would you answer "average rainfall from lo to hi" with the same prefix list?
